summary: Kits replace guests: auth, crawl, lake, neon, stripe and supabase link into a service's own program. Calls are metered and bounded by CPU time, databases by the size berm.toml gives them, and crab installs and upgrades itself from GitHub releases.
new: Link a kit into a service with #[berm_lang::program(uses = [...])]: its secrets, hosts and migrations join the service's manifest and its tables live in the service's database
Link kits through crabkit, a feature per kit: crabkit = { features = ["stripe"] } and uses = [crabkit::stripe]
Use the auth kit for accounts and sessions, stripe for checkout and subscriptions, supabase for PostgREST and Storage, and neon for Postgres over HTTP
Crawl the sites a service watches with the crawl kit: robots.txt and sitemaps, pages of the kinds it names, the URLs it lists and the links its crawler finds, recrawled when they change
Follow feeds and records with the lake kit: RSS 2.0, RSS 1.0 and Atom, threads under items, and a version stored per change of a record
Install crab with curl -fsSL https://crab.talk/install.sh | sh, and upgrade it in place with crab upgrade, each checked against GitHub's digest of the release asset
Start a service's database on Cloud from the seed berm.toml names, on its first deploy
Bound a service's database with [database] size in berm.toml, from 64KiB to 10GiB, 1GiB when unset
Subscribe from a trial at once with crab billing plan
Fetch many URLs in one call with berm_lang::http::fetch_all, each with its own timeout and the body bytes it takes
Declare fetch hosts as *.domain or *, a host reached only by a pattern refused at an address that is not public
Read random bytes with berm.random, and name the end user the rest of a call's chain runs for with berm.vouch
Run bermd with a development dashboard behind its dashboard feature, from ghcr.io/crabtalk/crab/berm or the repository's compose file
Build a product's services on crab with the crab skill in skills/crab
changed: Meter and bound each call by CPU time in microseconds in place of wasm instructions: budgets take cpu, and bermd takes --max-cpu-millis
Have crab new take berm-lang from crab's git tag of the CLI's release, its binary at bin/main.rs
Name a feed's Kind (chronological, unordered or records) in lake in place of its chronological flag, and give a listed item's posted as an Option, None when the feed gives no date
Collapse the crawl kit's migrations into one
Cut a response at the body bytes its request names in bermd, where it failed past 16MiB
Take Duration fields of berm_host::Config as "50ms" or "60s"
Move auth and stripe's services into fixtures, the kits staying libraries
Move berm_lang::html into the crab-html crate, which reads a page's title, meta, links and text
Drop the plan's storage rate, a plan's stored bytes the cap its services reserve against

Name the kit crates crabkit-auth, crabkit-crawl, crabkit-lake, crabkit-neon, crabkit-stripe and crabkit-supabase. A kit's migrations are recorded under its crate's name, so a database that ran them as crab-* runs them again and must be recreated
fixed: Read a fetch's host as the URL reaches it, so a URL spelled to look like another host, or an address written as a number, is held to the manifest and to bermd's public-address check
Bound every read of guest memory, so berm.random and berm.vouch cannot make the host allocate past it
Refuse a Supabase Storage path with an empty, . or .. segment, which reached another bucket
Hold the URLs a program lists to the site's robots.txt, match its * patterns in linear time, read it past a byte order mark, and compare its patterns percent-encoded
Keep a site's URLs when every sitemap fails, and split a round's shared sitemap budget so it cannot be overrun
Store an undated item and one posted at the watermark in a chronological feed, read nested RSS elements' text apart, and refuse out-of-range dates
End HTML tags at their real end and match tag names whole in crab-html, and keep an unknown entity as written
Refuse a database size under 64KiB, which left a database unlimited, and put the old size back when a deploy is refused
Show CPU in the dashboard, which broke on the renamed meter
Copy a deploy's seed through a temporary directory removed on every exit
